_doc: Curated DPRK / Contagious-Interview intel for DIRECT matching. Unlike the self-sourced infra set (hosts we confirmed ourselves), these are known-bad indicators matched directly, so a fresh sighting attributes on first contact instead of waiting for us to confirm it. Grounded in this tool's own confirmed cluster plus the publicly documented campaign structure. Keep specific: every entry must be something with near-zero legitimate use. Reviewed 2026-07-22.
_host_shape_doc: Regexes over a full host. The operator stands up disposable project subdomains on free PaaS. These are deliberately NOT bare 'vercel.app' (that is a legitimate service); they require the campaign's own naming shape so a normal deploy is never matched.
_path_shape_doc: The operator's dropper URL fingerprint: an OS-selector path segment plus a flag query, fetched and piped to a shell. This SURVIVES host rotation, so when they move to a new host the path still matches. Matched against the fetched URL in a curl/wget-to-shell line.
_package_families_doc: npm / pypi package-name families used as the malicious dependency in Contagious-Interview lures. Matched as an EXACT name or a documented family prefix; a range-versioned popular package is never confirmed on name alone (see manifest_scanner pinning).
_handle_doc: GitHub owner-handle heuristics are intentionally EMPTY. The cluster's victims are real developers with compromised accounts (kreliannn, teeps-heisenberg), so a handle pattern would brand victims. Attribution comes from code and infrastructure, never from who owns the repo.
